newsitem.title: FRANCE: Selling pressure hits French wheat, maize prices.
newsitem.headline: Selling pressure hits French wheat, maize prices.

text.p: French wheat and maize prices slipped further on Tuesday as grain cooperatives turned active sellers, dealers said.
Contributing to the decline in wheat prices were signs that one large grain cooperative from northern France was selling in anticipation that prices may ease further, they said.
"Sellers are trying to lighten their positions whenever they get the chance," one dealer said.
Wheat into Rouen was quoted at 840 francs per tonne for November delivery and at 835 francs on December delivery, both down five on Monday.
Volume was a slack 10 lots on MATIF wheat futures at 1420 GMT, with the February 1997 expiry quoted at 862 francs, down four francs on Monday
Maize eased as the harvest continued to make swift progress throughout France. This often creates a backlog at silos and forces cooperatives to try to sell their grain quickly, dealers said.
Fob Atlantic maize was offered at its Monday's bidding levels -- 870 francs for November delivery and 875 for January/March.
FOB Alsace maize for prompt delivery fetched 865 francs against 870 on Monday.
All grain prices exclude twice-monthly carrying charges.
